# USQualityCore ModelInfo 0.5.0

The CQL model of the US Quality Core 0.5.0 profiles, published as the `USQualityCore-ModelInfo` Library in `fhir.onc.us-quality-core` 0.5.0 and condensed here from its XML. A library uses it with `using USQualityCore version '0.5.0'`.

- **Model:** `USQualityCore`, URL `http://fhir.org/guides/onc/us-quality-core`, target `http://hl7.org/fhir`, qualifier `usqualitycore`
- **Requires:** System 1.0.0, FHIR 4.0.1, USCore 6.1.0-derived. This is a derived model: each class extends a USCore or FHIR class, so FHIR types, the FHIRHelpers conversions and the US Core libraries apply.
- **Patient class:** `USQualityCore.Patient`, birth date property `birthDate`
- **Contexts:** Practitioner (`USQualityCore.Practitioner`, key `id`); Device (`USQualityCore.Device`, key `id`); Patient (`USQualityCore.Patient`, key `id`); Encounter (`USQualityCore.Encounter`, key `id`); RelatedPerson (`USQualityCore.RelatedPerson`, key `id`)
- **Classes:** 65, plus 98 nested classes listed in their owner's file

Retrieve a class by name or by its quoted label. Declare `using FHIR` too, because the FHIRHelpers conversions don't apply without it. Most class names are also FHIR type names, so qualify them (`[USQualityCore.Encounter]`): with `using FHIR` declared, the unqualified name resolves to the FHIR type. A class with no primary code path needs an explicit code path in a terminology retrieve. In element types, `List<T>` is a repeating element and `Choice<A, B>` a choice element.
